title: Introduction to cleanr
text: first open real dataset, almost always run problems: missing values, messy column names, weird extreme numbers. cleanr gives three simple functions deal quickly.

title: Introduction to cleanr
text: cleanr comes built-dataset called messy_data three problems can practice.
code: messy_data #>   first_name last_name age  salary #> 1      Alice     Smith  25 5.0e+04 #> 2        Bob      <NA>  42 6.0e+04 #> 3       <NA>     Jones  31 5.5e+04 #> 4      Diana     Brown  28 1.0e+09 #> 5        Eve     Davis  NA 5.2e+04

title: Introduction to cleanr
text: shows exactly columns missing data much.
code: describe_na(messy_data) #>     variable n_missing pct_missing #> 1 first_name         1          20 #> 2  last_name         1          20 #> 3        age         1          20 #> 4     salary         0           0

title: Introduction to cleanr
text: Now names lowercase underscores, easy type.

title: Introduction to cleanr
text: salary one billion clearly wrong. can remove using IQR method:
code: clean <- remove_outliers(messy_data, col = "salary", method = "iqr") clean #>   first_name last_name age salary #> 1      Alice     Smith  25  50000 #> 2        Bob      <NA>  42  60000 #> 3       <NA>     Jones  31  55000 #> 5        Eve     Davis  NA  52000

title: Introduction to cleanr
code: result <- messy_data |>   remove_outliers(col = "salary", method = "iqr")  describe_na(result) #>     variable n_missing pct_missing #> 1 first_name         1          25 #> 2  last_name         1          25 #> 3        age         1          25 #> 4     salary         0           0

what: Tools for Data Cleaning and Validation
title: Tools for Data Cleaning and Validation
text: cleanr R package provides simple helper functions common data cleaning tasks. helps summarize missing values, standardize messy column names, remove outliers numeric columns.

title: Tools for Data Cleaning and Validation
Tools for Data Cleaning and Validation
code: library(cleanr)  # See missing values describe_na(messy_data) #>     variable n_missing pct_missing #> 1 first_name         1          20 #> 2  last_name         1          20 #> 3        age         1          20 #> 4     salary         0           0  # Clean column names df <- data.frame("First Name" = 1, "Last-Name!" = 2, check.names = FALSE) standardize_names(df) #>   first_name last_name #> 1          1         2  # Remove outliers df2 <- data.frame(x = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 100)) remove_outliers(df2, col = "x", method = "iqr") #>   x #> 1 1 #> 2 2 #> 3 3 #> 4 4
